main_text.p: Quæ nihil aliud est, quam ratio scienter ac rite tractandi gladium. Quam artem à Publio Rutilio Consule Cn. Manlii collegâ militibus tradi-tam asserit Valerius Maximus. Anno, inquit; ab urbe condita DCLVIII, nullius ante se Impe-ratoris exemplum secutus ex ludo C. Aurelii Scauri doctoribus gladiatorum accersitus, vitandi atque inferendi ictus subtilitatem, legibus ingeneravit. Quamquam hic Athen. Deipnos. libr.4.dissentiat Athenæus Deipno-sophista, qui hanc rudibus armis semet exercendi monomachiam, Hermippum Mantina-tum invenisse, & Cyrenæos æmulos fuisse, scribit. Sueton. in Cæsar. cap. 26.Quicquid sit de primis hujus artis inventoribus, id tamen certum est eam satis fuisse nobilita-tam, idque vel eo potissimum nomine, quod nobilissimi equites & Senatores Romani viri illustres ei operam dede-rint,

page.notes: The page number reads "48" (printed as 4·8). The numeral "IↃCLVIII" is read as DCLVIII (reversed C = D), giving the Latin "ab urbe condita DCLVIII". Left margin notes are positioned beside the lines they stand against: "Athen. Deipnos. libr.4.", "Sueton. in Cæsar. cap. 26.", and "Herod. in Commodo libr.1." (the last one is beside "est eam satis", where it is not yet written out in the note above; it should be added after "nobilita-" beside "est eam"). Hyphenated line-end words are written with their printed hyphens.
